# Results — Study 643 (Payrolls-Day-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **US
equities behave systematically on Nonfarm-Payrolls release mornings** (usually the first
Friday of the month, 8:30 am ET, the single most-watched print on the US macro calendar).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `7eebd76787d8` (SPY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY raw OHLC + adjusted close (7,419 rows), 1997-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| NFP calendar | **hardcoded** table of **353 actual Employment Situation release dates** 1997-01-10 → 2026-06-05 — the identical, source-verified table already used by sibling study [602-macro-announcement-premium](../../602-macro-announcement-premium/) (BLS archived-news-release index cross-checked against the official `histreleasedates.pdf`), trimmed to this study's as-of. Table starts 1997 rather than 1994 — extending it further back would mean re-deriving unverified dates instead of reusing the sourced ones |
| Release-day mapping | 353 of 353 releases land inside the SPY tape; **8** fell on a non-trading day (market holiday) and were forward-mapped to the next trading session — the session that actually prices the news |
| Events | all **353** release sessions sit on the tape, vs **7,065** other trading days |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group split (non-overlapping single-day events); **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the release-day dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw two-sided random-calendar placebo |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention (third axis only): the naive "own SPY only on NFP day" timer is entered at the **prior session's close** — the calendar is public months ahead, zero look-ahead — and exited at the release-day close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirks (named) | NFP lands at 8:30 am ET, **before** the 9:30 am open, so the release-day close-to-close bar fully contains the reaction (no intraday-only effect is missed). SPY is a total-return-friendly index vehicle — no survivorship on the Signal axis |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: SPY is an index-tracking ETF, not a survivor panel.
The naive timer on the third axis carries no survivorship either (single vehicle, no basket).

## The headline — release-day SPY return vs all other days

| quantity | release days | all other days |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean return | **+12.43 bps** | +3.37 bps |
| gap | **+9.06 bps** | |
| Welch *t* | **+1.31** | |
| Newey-West *t* (dummy regression, 5 lags) | **+1.31** | |
| hit rate (SPY up) | **206/353 = 58.4%** (Wilson 95% [53.2%, 63.4%]) vs a baseline up-day rate of **54.1%** on all other days | |

The point estimate is positive and roughly 3.7× the baseline daily drift, but the split does
**not** clear the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar either way (Welch or NW). **Random-calendar placebo:**
observed +12.43 bps vs placebo mean +3.33 bps (sd 6.31 bps) over **20,000 draws (20 seeds ×
1,000)**, two-sided → **p = 0.079** — a random calendar of 353 days produces something this
large about 8% of the time, comfortably inside the range chance explains. The hit-rate CI
[53.2%, 63.4%] barely clears the 54.1% baseline (SPY's long-run up-day rate on ordinary days
is already above 50%) — not the clean directional edge the folklore implies.

## Event window — pre-release drift and persistence (mean return in bps, Welch *t* vs far-from-release days)

| offset | −3 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean bps | +6.10 | **+17.05** | −2.05 | **+12.43** | −7.16 | +0.67 | −4.90 |
| Welch *t* | +0.30 | **+2.08** | −0.93 | +1.19 | −1.60 | −0.53 | −1.30 |

- **Pre-release drift:** the cumulative [−3..−1] window is **+21.10 bps/event** at one-sample
  *t* = **+2.07**, and offset −2 alone nominally clears *t* = 2.08. Both are flagged, not
  certified: this is **1 of 7 offsets tested here with no multiple-comparison correction**,
  exactly the kind of post-hoc pattern the desk's snooping rule exists to catch. It is a
  genuine hint worth its own pre-registered study — not evidence banked on the Signal axis of
  *this* one.
- **The release day itself:** +12.43 bps at *t* = 1.19 (weaker than the *pooled* headline
  split above, which uses the full non-overlapping sample rather than the windowed
  subset — the two numbers are close but not identical by construction).
- **No clean persistence story:** day +1 is *negative* (−7.16 bps, *t* = −1.60) — if anything
  a mild, uncertified give-back, not a continuation.

## Realized SPY range on the same days — mechanically louder mornings

| metric | release days | other days | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY (H−L)/prev close | **1.474%** | 1.342% | **+2.50** |

Unlike the return itself, the **realized range clears the bar**: NFP mornings are
measurably noisier than an average session — exactly the resolution-of-scheduled-uncertainty
signature the desk's FOMC vol-crush study (637) found on Fed decision days. The market moves
*more* on release day; it just doesn't move in a statistically certified *direction*.

## Era contrast — pre vs post 2013 (justified split: sample midpoint, roughly the post-crisis-normalization/QE-taper era)

| era | NFP-day return | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1997 → 2013 | +13.58 bps | 192 | +1.16 |
| 2013 → 2026 | +11.06 bps | 161 | +0.63 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | **−0.19** |

Neither era alone clears *t* ≥ 2, and the (small, noisy) apparent decline between eras is
itself statistically indistinguishable from zero (*t* = −0.19). No decay to report — there
was nothing certified to decay from.

## Third axis — the naive timer: own SPY only on the NFP release day

Enter the prior close (calendar public months ahead — zero look-ahead), exit the release-day
close; 353 scheduled releases, 1997 → 2026.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| gross per event | **+12.43 bps** |
| net per event (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **+2.43 / −7.57 bps** (~ +0.29% / −0.91%/yr at 12 events) |
| all-other-days SPY mean | +3.37 bps |
| Welch *t* (NFP vs other days) | **+1.31** (already sub-bar before costs) |
| hit rate | 58.4% |
| worst single release day | **−6.0%** |

The gross edge is uncertified to begin with (*t* = 1.31), and it does not survive realistic
one-way costs: at 5 bps the net contribution is a rounding error (+0.29%/yr from twelve
trades a year); at 10 bps it is outright negative. A single bad release morning (−6.0%) can
erase years of the "edge." There is no residual to allocate capital to.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic random-walk daily return series with scheduled pseudo-release days every 21st
business day and a TUNABLE planted release-day effect; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.16** (sd 1.20), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** (consistent with a ~5%-level two-sided test's expected false-positive rate; not systematically biased) |
| planted edge = +15 bps/day (seed 643) | **+2.46** |

The detector recovers a planted effect of roughly the observed real-tape magnitude and does
not manufacture significance out of a null world at an unusual rate. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Release-day SPY return **+12.43 bps** vs +3.37 bps on all other days:
  Welch *t* = **+1.31**, Newey-West *t* = **+1.31**, random-calendar placebo **p = 0.079**
  (two-sided) — none clear the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar. Hit rate 58.4% (Wilson [53.2%, 63.4%])
  barely clears the 54.1% baseline SPY already carries on ordinary days. A nominal pre-release
  drift (cumulative [−3..−1] *t* = +2.07) is named honestly as an uncorrected, exploratory hit
  among seven offsets tested — a hint, not a certified finding.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even taking the uncertified point estimate at face value, the
  naive "own SPY only on NFP day" timer nets **+2.43 bps/event at 5 bps** (~+0.29%/yr) and
  goes **net negative at 10 bps** (−7.57 bps, ~−0.91%/yr); worst single release day **−6.0%**.
  There is no edge left once costs and a normal bad day are on the table.
- **"Louder, not directional?" — CONFIRMED.** The realized SPY high-low range on release days
  clears the bar decisively (**1.474%** vs 1.342%, Welch *t* = **+2.50**) — NFP mornings are
  genuinely, mechanically noisier. But that loudness never translates into a certified
  directional edge (Signal *t* = 1.31; Tradability = Mirage). The folklore is right that
  something happens on payrolls Friday; it is wrong that you can bank *which way*.
